vulnerability_type: ROOT VALIDATION (verified secure - NOT a vulnerability)
description: The #1 catastrophic privacy-pool bug (attacker-chosen Merkle root) is NOT present. transact() feeds `root` into the Groth16 public inputs at lib.rs:3644, verifies the proof at 3653, then REQUIRES the root to be a known historical root of the on-chain input tree at lib.rs:3656: `require!(MerkleTree::is_known_root(&*input_tree, root), PrivacyError::UnknownRoot)`. The input_tree account is a PDA seeded by [b"privacy_note_tree_v3", mint_address, input_tree_id] (lib.rs:742-747), so the attacker cannot substitute a foreign/fabricated tree. is_known_root (merkle_tree.rs:116-148) rejects the zero root and walks the 256-entry root_history ring buffer, returning true ONLY on an exact match with a genuinely stored root; there is no code path that accepts an unknown root. Root is also require_canonical'd (< Fr) in zk.rs:173 so the byte encoding is unique. An attacker therefore cannot prove membership of a self-controlled commitment against an arbitrary root.
attack_scenario: N/A - attempted attack: pass an attacker-computed root that commits to a note the attacker controls, prove membership, and withdraw. Blocked: is_known_root only matches roots the program itself appended via MerkleTree::append, and the tree is a mint-bound PDA.
impact: None. Pool cannot be drained via forged root.
recommendation: No change required. (Minor non-security note: merkle_tree.rs line 8/EXPECTED_SIZE=9107 and the stale '26 * 32' test comment vs MERKLE_TREE_HEIGHT=22 are cosmetic/layout-doc drift, not exploitable.)
poc_outline: N/A - control verified present and correct.

vulnerability_type: NULLIFIER DOUBLE-SPEND (verified secure - NOT a vulnerability)
description: Double-spend is prevented at account-resolution time. Each input nullifier gets a dedicated PDA marker created with Anchor `init` (NOT init_if_needed) seeded by [b"nullifier_v3", mint_address, input_nullifier_N] (lib.rs:768-788). `init` fails if the PDA already exists, so a re-used nullifier aborts the tx before any state change, and this is atomic across concurrent txs (only one can create the PDA). Markers are GLOBAL (no tree_id in seeds), preventing cross-tree reuse. transact() additionally rejects equal nullifiers (3492) and zero nullifiers (3494-3496), and defensively checks !is_spent (3666-3667) before mark_nullifier_spent sets is_spent=true (4908). Nullifiers are require_canonical'd (< Fr, zk.rs:174-175) so the raw 32-byte PDA seed is 1:1 with the field element bound by the proof - no two byte-encodings collide to bypass the marker. State-change ordering is safe: proof + root + marker init all precede any fund movement in handle_public_amount.
attack_scenario: N/A - attempted attacks (reuse same nullifier, two concurrent txs, both nullifiers equal, zero nullifier, non-canonical alias) are all rejected.
code_snippet:
// lib.rs:768-775
#[account(init, payer = relayer,
  seeds = [b"nullifier_v3", mint_address.as_ref(), input_nullifier_0.as_ref()],
  bump, space = NullifierMarker::LEN)]
pub nullifier_marker_0: Account<'info, NullifierMarker>,
poc_outline: N/A - control verified present and correct.

vulnerability_type: EXT DATA / RECIPIENT & RELAYER BINDING (verified secure - NOT a vulnerability)
description: Fee-redirection / front-running is prevented. transact() recomputes the ext-data hash on-chain from the caller-supplied ExtData (recipient, relayer, fee, refund, claimant) via ExtData::hash() and requires it to equal the ext_data_hash argument (lib.rs:3514-3515), which is itself a bound Groth16 public input (zk.rs:189). It then binds the ACTUAL accounts to the hashed values: relayer signer == ext_data.relayer (3533-3537), recipient == ext_data.recipient (3540-3544), and for token withdrawals recipient_token.owner == ext_data.recipient and relayer_token.owner == ext_data.relayer (3628-3638). Because ext_data_hash is a proof public input, a relayer/front-runner cannot swap in their own recipient/relayer without invalidating the proof. ExtData::hash reduces pubkeys mod Fr and Poseidon-hashes Poseidon(recipient,relayer), Poseidon(fee,refund), claimant (lib.rs:538-551); the claimant field (AUDIT-005) additionally binds the ephemeral claim key.
attack_scenario: N/A - attempted attack: malicious relayer substitutes its own recipient/relayer accounts to steal a withdrawal. Blocked by the on-chain hash recomputation + account-equality checks against proof-bound ext_data_hash.
poc_outline: N/A - control verified present and correct.

vulnerability_type: ACCOUNTING / publicAmount CONSERVATION (verified secure - NOT a vulnerability)
description: publicAmount is a single i64 used BOTH as the proof public input (zk.rs:186 i64_to_field_be, correctly encoding negatives as Fr-|x|) and as the on-chain transfer amount (handle_public_amount), so the value moved always equals the value the circuit proved (sumIns + publicAmount = sumOuts). Sign handling is correct: >0 deposit (user->vault), <0 withdrawal (vault->recipient+relayer), ==0 private transfer. Withdrawal uses unsigned_abs() to avoid i64::MIN overflow (5000). Fee/refund are constrained: deposits/transfers force fee==refund==0 (4963,5164-5167); withdrawals enforce fee+refund <= withdrawal (5015-5016), to_recipient via checked_sub (5019-5022), fee within [min_withdrawal_fee, max_fee*(1+margin)] (5043-5064), and min-withdrawal-for-fee floor (5029-5039). All arithmetic uses checked_add/sub/mul; TVL updated with checked ops. Vault-side balance is verified sufficient before payout in both token (5074-5077) and SOL (5117-5125, incl. rent-exempt + 0.01 SOL buffer) paths. A withdrawal cannot move more than the proof authorizes, and value is conserved across recipient+relayer+remaining-notes.
attack_scenario: N/A - attempted attacks (withdraw more than deposited, sign confusion, fee/refund underflow to inflate payout) all blocked by the shared i64, checked arithmetic, and fee<=withdrawal bounds.
poc_outline: N/A - control verified present and correct.

vulnerability_type: TOKEN vs SOL CONFUSION & VAULT AUTHORITY/PDA SUBSTITUTION (verified secure - NOT a vulnerability)
description: Mint, vault, and vault-ATA are all bound to config, and the vault is a program-signed PDA. transact() requires mint_address == config.mint_address (3547). is_token_mint(mint) (827) selects the token vs native-SOL path off that config-bound mint, so an attacker cannot deposit a worthless SPL token and withdraw SOL: the pool is single-mint and effective_mint/is_token_mint derive from config.mint_address only. For SPL pools it enforces token_program == token::ID (3555), vault_token_account == canonical ATA(vault, config.mint_address) (3566-3575), vault_token.mint == config.mint_address (3578), and vault_token.owner == vault PDA (3581-3585). deserialize_token_account (833-841) rejects any account not owned by the SPL Token program before use, blocking fake/attacker token-account substitution. Withdrawal CPIs are signed by the vault PDA with seeds [b"privacy_vault_v3", config.mint_address, vault.bump] (5088,5105); the SOL path manipulates lamports directly on the vault PDA the program owns (5131-5145). The vault account itself is a PDA seeded [b"privacy_vault_v3", mint_address] bump=config.vault_bump (lib.rs:734-739), so it cannot be swapped for an attacker account.
attack_scenario: N/A - attempted attacks (pass attacker-controlled token account as vault, wrong-mint ATA, deposit cheap token / withdraw SOL, substitute non-ATA vault) all blocked by ATA derivation check, mint/owner checks, SPL-owner check, and PDA seed constraints.
poc_outline: N/A - control verified present and correct.

vulnerability_type: Loss of funds / permanently locked collateral (position-note vs PositionPDA decoupling)
line_range: 1031-1419, 1424-1798 (change-note append at 1265-1274 and 1625-1634); PDA creators at open_position:1329-1336 and merge_positions:1730-1737
description: Position value is held in ZK notes in the position Merkle tree, but a note can only ever be *spent* (closed/merged) if a matching PositionPDA exists at seeds [b"position_pda_v1", poseidon(note_secret)]. A PositionPDA is created in exactly two places: open_position (for the freshly opened position note) and merge_positions (for the single merged output note). The swap circuit used by close_position / close_position_to_sol emits TWO output commitments: output_commitment_1 = the swapped-out proceeds note (USDC/SOL, deposited into a note-based pool where it is freely spendable) and output_commitment_0 = a *position change note* re-inserted into the position tree (append_and_emit at positions.rs:1265 and :1625). On a PARTIAL close (swap_amount < full note value) this change note carries the remaining position value, yet NO PositionPDA is created for it and the spent position's PDA is closed (close = relayer). Because close_position/close_position_to_sol/merge_positions all require an already-initialized PositionPDA (Anchor `bump = position_pda.bump`, non-init) keyed by the note secret, the orphaned change note can never be closed or merged again. The remaining collateral in the shared per-mint position vault becomes permanently unspendable.
attack_scenario: A user (or relayer acting for a user) opens a position note worth V of a meme token (PositionPDA_A created, V meme in the shared position vault). They later submit close_position with swap_amount = V/2 (a valid partial close the swap circuit supports: change note = V - swap_amount). The tx succeeds: note A is nullified, PDA_A is closed to the relayer, V/2 meme is swapped out to a spendable USDC/SOL note, and a change note worth V/2 is appended to the position tree. That change note has a fresh secret => a fresh position_pda_key for which no account was ever `init`ed. Any subsequent close_position/close_position_to_sol/merge_positions for it fails at the Accounts stage (`seeds ... bump = position_pda.bump` on a non-existent account), so the V/2 of vault collateral is stranded forever.
impact: Permanent loss of access to the residual collateral of any partially-closed position. No attacker profit (funds are locked, not stolen), and no cross-user theft, but user funds backing an orphaned change note are unrecoverable. Severity is bounded by whether the relayer/client ever issues partial closes; the circuit and on-chain code both permit them, so the failure mode is reachable.
recommendation: Either (a) forbid partial closes explicitly (require swap_amount equals the full note value / require the change note to be a canonical zero-value note), or (b) create a PositionPDA for the change note inside close_position/close_position_to_sol (init a new_position_pda keyed by the change note secret, mirroring merge_positions' new_position_pda), so the remaining position value stays spendable. If partial closes are intentionally unsupported, document and enforce it on-chain rather than relying on client behavior.
poc_outline: 1. init_position_pool + fund a meme mint vault via open_position, producing PositionPDA_A (balance V) and V meme in position_vault_ata. 2. Build a SwapProof for a partial close: input note A (value V), swap_amount = V/2, output_commitment_0 = change note (value V/2, new secret S'), output_commitment_1 = USDC/SOL proceeds note. 3. Call close_position: assert it succeeds, PDA_A is closed, change note appended to position tree. 4. Attempt close_position (or merge_positions) for note S': derive position_pda_key = poseidon(S'); show the required PositionPDA account does not exist and cannot be created by any instruction => tx fails at account resolution. 5. Conclude the V/2 vault collateral is unspendable.

description: phoenix_deposit_from_pool pins the EMBER/PhUSD system accounts to their canonical addresses before the EMBER CPI (phoenix.rs:376-378: remaining[8]==PHUSD_MINT_AUTHORITY, remaining[9]==PHUSD_MINT, remaining[11]==EMBER_USDC_RESERVE). The two standalone EMBER paths do NOT replicate these pins. phoenix_ember_wrap only checks remaining[0]==EMBER_PROGRAM_ID (line 1350) and then passes remaining[1] (phUsdMintAuthPda), remaining[2] (usdcMint), remaining[3] (phUsdMint) and remaining[4] (emberUsdcReserve) into the EMBER deposit CPI unvalidated (lines 1391-1396). phoenix_ember_unwrap only pins remaining[0]==PHOENIX and remaining[9]==EMBER (lines 1473-1474) and passes remaining[10..13] (phUsdMintAuthPda, usdcMint, phUsdMint, emberUsdcReserve) into the EMBER withdraw CPI unvalidated (lines 1611-1616). Both structs (PhoenixEmberWrap lib.rs:2191, PhoenixEmberUnwrap lib.rs:2233) require only the relayer to sign - there is no claimant co-signer on these two instructions - so the substitutable accounts are fully caller-controlled by whoever holds the relayer key.
attack_scenario: A compromised or malicious relayer calls phoenix_ember_wrap for a claimant whose executor USDC ATA currently holds a balance and substitutes remaining[4] (emberUsdcReserve) with an attacker-controlled token account. If the external EMBER program does not itself validate that the passed reserve/mint/authority are its own canonical accounts, EMBER would move the executor's USDC to the attacker's substituted 'reserve' while still minting canonical PhUSD to the executor, redirecting pool-derived USDC. The deposit handler was explicitly hardened against exactly this (it pins all three EMBER system accounts), which indicates the design intent is NOT to trust the relayer with these addresses; the wrap/unwrap paths silently break that invariant.
impact: Potential redirection of executor-held (pool-derived) USDC to an attacker account under a malicious-relayer threat model. NOTE: exploitability is CONDITIONAL and unconfirmed - it requires BOTH (a) the external EMBER program (EMBERpYNE6...) to omit internal validation of its own reserve/mint-authority accounts, which a correctly implemented peg wrapper would not do, AND (b) a malicious/compromised relayer. The canonical-mint ATA validations on executor_ph_usd_ata / executor_token_account (lines 1362-1375, 1489-1502) already block phUsdMint / destination substitution. Reported as a hardening gap, not a confirmed drain.
recommendation: Mirror the deposit handler's pins in both standalone EMBER paths: add require_keys_eq! that remaining[1..4] (ember_wrap) and remaining[10..13] (ember_unwrap) equal PHUSD_MINT_AUTHORITY, PHOENIX_REQUIRED_MINT, PHUSD_MINT and EMBER_USDC_RESERVE respectively. This makes the CPI account set relayer-independent and consistent with phoenix_deposit_from_pool.
poc_outline: 1. Fund an executor USDC ATA (e.g., mid-flow or via a partial deposit). 2. As the relayer, call phoenix_ember_wrap with remaining[4]=attacker_usdc_account. 3. Observe whether EMBER routes the executor USDC to the substituted account. If EMBER validates its reserve internally the CPI reverts (no exploit); if not, USDC is redirected. This PoC is the decisive test of exploitability and should be run against EMBER on a fork before treating it as more than a hardening item.

vulnerability_type: Broken proof binding / unauthenticated swap instruction data (documented security invariant not enforced)
description: SwapParams carries a `swap_data_hash` field whose documented purpose (lines 53-58) is: 'Binds the exact DEX instruction bytes into the ZK proof so the relayer cannot substitute different swap_data (e.g. 0% slippage) after the user has generated their proof.' However, `SwapParams::hash()` (lines 102-127) computes swap_params_hash from ONLY source_mint, dest_mint, min_amount_out, deadline and dest_amount. It never hashes `self.swap_data_hash`. swap_params_hash is the sole swap-params value bound into the Groth16 proof (public_inputs[1] in zk.rs verify_swap_transaction_groth16, line 276). Therefore `swap_params.swap_data_hash` is NOT committed to by the ZK proof. In transact_swap's Jupiter branch the only integrity gate on the raw Jupiter route bytes is `require!(sha256(swap_data) == swap_params.swap_data_hash)` (lines 827-828). Since BOTH `swap_data` and `swap_params.swap_data_hash` are relayer-controlled instruction arguments and neither is proof-bound, this check is self-referential and enforces nothing about the user's intent: the relayer can pick any swap_data and set swap_data_hash = sha256(that swap_data). The documented anti-substitution guarantee for Jupiter routes does not exist.
attack_scenario: A user generates a swap proof authorizing a Jupiter route (implicitly committing to swap_data_hash so the relayer cannot re-route). A malicious/compromised whitelisted relayer discards the user-supplied swap_data and substitutes its own Jupiter route bytes (e.g. a path through a pool the relayer controls or is sandwiching), and sets swap_params.swap_data_hash = sha256(substituted bytes). The proof still verifies because swap_params_hash does not cover swap_data_hash. The substituted route executes. The output still lands in executor_dest_token (dest account forced by the account substitution at indices 1/2/3 or 2/3/6), and swap.rs line 849 still enforces swapped_amount >= swap_params.min_amount_out (min_amount_out IS proof-bound), so extraction is capped at the user's slippage budget rather than being unbounded.
impact: For transact_swap the loss is bounded by the user's proof-bound min_amount_out check (line 849): a substituting relayer can degrade execution / extract value only down to min_amount_out, and cannot touch other users' pool funds. This is the loss of a documented defense-in-depth layer, not unbounded theft — hence medium, not high. IMPORTANT cross-impact: SwapParams::hash is shared with the position pool (positions.rs execute_dex_swap line 1907 and the staged-legs cosigner path lines 774-810/1895-1908) where swap output first lands in an attacker-influenced ephemeral COSIGNER account and is swept via a relayer-authored legs blob whose only gate is this same broken swap_data_hash check; that path should be re-audited by the positions-cluster analyst for a potentially higher-severity variant.
recommendation: Include swap_data_hash in the swap_params_hash preimage (e.g. add reduce_to_field(swap_data_hash) as an input to the Poseidon hash in SwapParams::hash), AND update the off-chain circuit so the witness's swap_data_hash is constrained into swapParamsHash. This makes swap_data_hash genuinely proof-bound so a relayer cannot substitute Jupiter route bytes. Alternatively, decode and enforce Jupiter's in-amount/min-out on-chain the way the CPMM/AMM branches already do (lines 546-557, 640-650) instead of relying on the hash.
poc_outline: 1) User builds a valid swap proof for a Jupiter route with swap_data D and correct swap_data_hash=sha256(D), min_amount_out=M (M proof-bound). 2) Relayer replaces D with D' (adversarial route/slippage) and sets swap_params.swap_data_hash=sha256(D'). 3) Call transact_swap; verify_swap_transaction_groth16 passes because swap_params_hash omits swap_data_hash. 4) require(sha256(D')==sha256(D')) passes at line 828; D' executes. 5) Confirm the swap executed on the relayer's substituted route while proof only ever authorized D — demonstrating swap_data is unbound. Add a unit test asserting SwapParams::hash() output is invariant to changing swap_data_hash to prove the omission.
